problem: Existing VLN agents build their environment representations (hidden states, topological graphs, BEV/grid semantic maps) from 2D perspective features extracted by monocular encoders. This compresses depth onto the image plane and drops the height dimension, so they miss 3D geometry and semantics in complex, occluded indoor scenes.
motivation: Decisions in VLN depend on holistic scene understanding, and BEV maps already help, but they flatten vertical structure. Autonomous-driving work on BEV and 3D-occupancy perception shows that multi-view 2D features can be lifted into a structured voxel space and supervised with 3D perception tasks. The authors argue that such a complete 3D representation should give better language grounding and action prediction than 2D or planar maps.
key_idea: Lift the multi-view panoramic features at each step into a voxel grid (VER) using BEVFormer-style deformable cross-view attention, pretrain it with coarse-to-fine multi-task 3D perception (occupancy, 3D boxes, room layout), then navigate by combining language-conditioned 'volume state' transition probabilities over voxels with a topological episodic memory whose nodes are built from voxel pillars.
insight: The two navigation modules each matter substantially (Table 4, val-unseen). Removing episodic memory drops R2R SR from 75.80 to 68.21 and REVERIE SR from 55.98 to 49.33. Removing volume-state estimation drops them to 72.71 and 52.31. The 3D supervision itself contributes smaller but consistent gains (Table 8, R2R val-unseen SR). Occupancy alone gives 74.90 SR and all three tasks give 75.80. Dropping occupancy (boxes + layout only) is worst at 74.03, so dense occupancy is the most useful signal. Learnable 3D-deconvolution upsampling beats trilinear interpolation (SR 75.14→75.80; occupancy mIoU 11.03→12.93). A 3×3 neighborhood (|Ω|=9) around each candidate is the sweet spot: smaller lacks context, larger adds irrelevant voxels.
method: Environment encoder (2D-3D sampling): 15×15×4 learnable volume queries covering [-6,6] m in x-y and [-1.5,2] m in height are projected into each ImageNet ViT-B/16 view feature using camera intrinsics/extrinsics. Six layers of deformable cross-view attention (CVA, S=6 sampling points) aggregate these views into a voxel feature F3d (D=768).

Coarse-to-fine VER extraction: M=3 cascaded 3D deconvolutions upsample the coarse volume, and each level re-queries the 2D features with CVA. Every scale is supervised with multi-resolution labels (0.4/0.2/0.1 m voxels, 120×120×35 at the finest).

Multi-task 3D perception pretraining: an MLP occupancy head (focal loss), a query-based Manhattan room-layout head (L1 + IoU loss) and a BEVFormer-style 3D detection head (bipartite matching), weighted 2.0/0.25/0.25. Labels are auto-generated from Matterport3D point clouds via a room-object-voxel pipeline (~50B voxels, 16 classes, ~100k boxes, 1,500 layouts). The encoder is frozen during navigation.

Volume state estimation: the voxel grid is split into height-aware groups (one XY slice per z level). A shared 4-layer transformer (LXMERT-initialized) jointly encodes each slice with the instruction embeddings. An MLP + softmax then gives transition probabilities over all voxels. These are averaged over height, summed within a 9-cell neighborhood of each candidate viewpoint (and the current node for STOP), and trained with a Gaussian-heatmap focal loss.

Episodic memory / global action: an online topological graph stores node embeddings obtained by average-pooling the neighboring voxel pillars (|Ω|×Z) of each observed viewpoint, averaged for revisited nodes. A transformer over [instruction; nodes] gives global action probabilities, fused with the local probabilities via a learnable weight W_g. Backtrack entries reuse the local STOP probability.

Training: HAMT/DUET-style pretraining with MLM + SAP (+ Object Grounding on REVERIE) on offline-sampled instruction-route pairs (batch 64, 100k iterations), then DAgger fine-tuning (0.25·teacher-forcing + student-forcing + OG loss; lr 1e-5, 20k iterations). For REVERIE, object features are concatenated into each height group for object grounding.

setting.backbone: ImageNet ViT-B/16 image features + BEVFormer-style deformable-attention voxel encoder (pretrained on 3D perception, frozen) + LXMERT-initialized 4-layer transformers (fine-tuned); trained in-house
setting.training_data: R2R / REVERIE / R4R training data plus offline-sampled (augmented) instruction-route pairs for pretraining (following hao2020towards). Separately, auto-generated 3D perception annotations on Matterport3D (occupancy ~50B voxels / 16 classes, ~100k 3D boxes, 1,500 room layouts; R2R scene splits) for the environment encoder.
setting.observation: panoramic multi-view RGB images with known camera intrinsics/extrinsics (no depth input; 3D labels only used for training the encoder)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (local candidates + global jump/backtrack to any observed node in the topological graph, plus STOP)

numbers_note: The paper also reports 3D perception results on its own auto-generated Matterport3D annotations (Table 6; split not stated): occupancy IoU 24.31 / mIoU 12.93, detection mAP 33.57 / mAR 51.60, layout 3D IoU 66.45. These beat BEVFormer and OccNet. They are not listed as navigation entries. Ablation Table 4 gives the full model's more precise R2R val-unseen values: SR 75.80, SPL 65.37.
results: On R2R test the model reaches SR 76 / SPL 66 (NE 2.74), versus 73/62 for BEVBert. On REVERIE val-unseen it reaches SR 55.98 / SPL 39.66, +3.86 / +4.07 over BSG. On REVERIE test it gets SR 56.82 / SPL 38.76. Object-grounding metrics do not beat the strongest baselines: val-unseen RGS 33.71 vs BSG 35.36, and test RGS 33.88 vs GridMM 34.87. On R4R val-unseen it gets SR 47 (ties BSG), CLS 61, nDTW 54, but SDTW 33 is below BSG's 34.
limitations: Trained and evaluated only in static Matterport3D discrete-graph VLN. The authors note that moving objects are not handled and that transfer to continuous (VLN-CE), aerial or other navigation tasks is untested.
Needs dense 3D supervision (occupancy, boxes, layouts) derived from Matterport3D point clouds and meshes, plus calibrated camera poses. This limits scaling to scenes without such reconstructions.

Gains come mainly in navigation SR/SPL. Remote-grounding metrics on REVERIE (RGS/RGSPL) fall behind BSG, BEVBert and GridMM. The multi-task 3D supervision itself adds only about 1 SR point over occupancy-only training.
